breaking_changes: Removed the --no-sign flag from the release tagging tool; omit the flag (now the default) or use --sign for signed tags.

checklist.author: @abn
checklist.text: On a Linux or macOS desktop without lemond running, launch lemonade-tray with --spawn-server and verify that lemond starts within 15 seconds, the tray menu populates, and quitting the tray causes lemond to terminate immediately without leaving an orphan process.

checklist.author: @RaulMermans
checklist.text: Run lemonade config set flm.flm_bin=builtin and confirm it returns an Unknown key error, then run lemonade config set flm.npu_bin=builtin and confirm it succeeds.

checklist.author: @ramkrishna2910
checklist.text: On a macOS release candidate, run lemonade-tray --spawn-server and confirm stderr prints 'Warning: --spawn-server is not supported on macOS and will be ignored.' and that the tray launches in disconnected mode without starting a local lemond.

checklist.author: @Copilot
checklist.text: Run the release tagging tool in dry-run mode and confirm the output says 'would create and push annotated tag' rather than 'signed tag'.

checklist.author: @Copilot
checklist.text: Run the release tagging tool with the --sign flag in dry-run mode and confirm the output says 'would create and push signed tag'.

evidence.blockers: No blockers. The three P1 to-dos cover new user-visible surface (tray spawn-server on POSIX, config validation tightening, spawn-server warning on macOS) and two P2 items for internal release-tooling. All CI passed on merge.
evidence.breaking_changes: The release tagging tool removed --no-sign and made unsigned tags the default; operators using --no-sign must drop it. No end-user API or config changes break existing setups.
evidence.coverage: Reviewed all 14 commits in the release bucket from v2026.40.0 to 16bcf63. Five to-dos from three commits carry forward; the remaining nine commits had no testable to-dos (documentation-only changes, version bumps, or internal refactors).
evidence.manual_testing: Tray spawn-server end-to-end on a real Linux/macOS desktop (PR #3304), macOS --spawn-server warning path (PR #3687), and config validation through lemonade CLI (PR #3684) were not exercised by automated tests before merge.
evidence.security: No security-relevant observations. The watchdog pipe FD_CLOEXEC semantics are sound (PR #3304), the macOS spawn-server guard is strictly more restrictive (PR #3687), and the config validation tightening is a defensive improvement (PR #3684).
